strengths: Well-motivated contribution: Compelling argument that LLMs waste capability on uninformative boundary timestamps and should leverage semantic understanding instead
Comprehensive evaluation: Multiple benchmarks (E.T.Bench with 9 tasks, Charades-STA, QVHighlights), detailed ablations (Tables 4-6), and zero-shot with controlled data leakage
Strong empirical results: Substantial gains across domains (59.1% vs 44.3% on TVG_F1, 43.4% vs 39.7% on DVC_F1) using smaller model than competitors
Thorough ablation studies: Tables 5-6 clearly demonstrate necessity of both structural tokens and query-focused captioning; Table 3 provides semantic justification
Good reproducibility: Detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, supplementary material, promised code release
Clear presentation: Intuitive problem framing ('measure twice, cut once'), good visual illustrations, comprehensive related work positioning
weaknesses: Query-Focused Captioning concerns: Relies entirely on external models (MiniCPM-V2.6 + GPT-4o-mini) for caption generation with no human evaluation, quality analysis, or sensitivity studies; error propagation from these models not addressed

Multi-segment generalization is ad-hoc: QVHighlights results use simple thresholding without prior multi-segment training; threshold selection unjustified and not ablated; appears to be a significant leap from structural token training
Methodological data usage concerns: QFC generation uses ground-truth event timestamps; extensive segment boundary usage during training despite claims of zero-shot evaluation

Limited technical novelty: Structural token grounding is straightforward application of existing contrastive learning; main contribution is motivation and combination rather than novel techniques; asymmetric loss choice not investigated
Incomplete failure analysis: Only successful cases shown (Figure 3); no systematic error characterization or analysis of when/why method fails compared to baselines

Missing computational analysis: No discussion of training time, inference latency, or memory overhead; QFC pipeline adds multiple inference calls (caption model + GPT) during data preparation; scalability not addressed

Insufficient justification for design choices: 1 fps sampling, 1 epoch training, LoRA rank 128 lack sensitivity analysis or rationale; extensive prompt engineering (GPT-4o diversification) raises robustness questions

Key assumptions under-validated: Relies on video LLMs having 'excellent temporal structure understanding' but provides limited direct evidence for this task; transition token modeling clarity—do <tst> tokens capture diverse semantics or just generic background?
Evaluation nuances: Charades-STA shows marginal improvements on R@10.7; gray-shaded metrics indicate non-zero-shot results; simplified single-segment E.T.Bench evaluation reduces difficulty
Comparison fairness: TRACE uses 900K samples, 2 epochs, full fine-tuning vs. MeCo's 164K, 1 epoch, LoRA; while Table 1 addresses this, confounds remain

strengths: Well-motivated core contribution: compelling argument that semantic-oriented approach better leverages LLMs' capabilities compared to timestamp generation, with clear conceptual innovation

Comprehensive and rigorous empirical evaluation: 9 diverse tasks across E.T. Bench, Charades-STA, and QVHighlights with both zero-shot and fine-tuning results; consistent improvements across most metrics
Thorough ablation studies: Table 5-7 provide detailed analysis of component necessity and design choices; Table 4 ensures fair comparisons with controlled base models and frame sampling
Strong empirical results: substantial gains on many metrics (e.g., TVG F1: 62.5 vs previous 44.3), excellent performance on highlight detection, and good scalability with larger LLMs
Excellent reproducibility: detailed implementation details, complete inference pseudocode, training/evaluation templates, and promised code release with supplementary data
Clear and honest presentation: well-structured paper with effective visualizations, compelling motivation, and candid discussion of limitations (fine-grained metric trade-offs)
weaknesses: Limited component-level novelty: structural tokens are simple special tokens, query-focused captioning is straightforward caption generation, token grounding uses standard contrastive learning; contribution primarily lies in combination rather than individual innovation

Dependency on external caption generation: requires MiniCPM-V-2.6 and GPT-4o-mini; creates error propagation risk, lacks analysis of caption quality impact, and introduces practical barriers for reproducibility

Circular use of ground-truth boundaries: training data synthesis uses ground-truth event boundaries from E.T.Instruct to generate query-focused captions, creating potential data leakage and making training efficiency claims less clean

Acknowledged trade-off with fine-grained localization: R@10.7 performance substantially lower than competitors (19.1% vs 24.0% for VideoChat-T); fundamental semantic-oriented limitation with no proposed solution limits applicability

Incomplete computational analysis: no inference time comparisons provided; caption generation per event could be significantly slower than direct timestamp generation, with real-time implications unaddressed
Limited generalization study: experiments confined to E.T.Chat and QWen2VL architectures; three-stage training is E.T.Chat-specific; generalization to other video LLM architectures unclear

Methodological inelegance: asymmetric contrastive loss (only p(h_t|s_i)) lacks principled justification despite empirical success; Table 6 shows symmetric version fails, suggesting potential optimization issues
Statistical rigor gaps: no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; single-run results; some improvements are modest (2-3 F1 points on certain tasks)

strengths: Well-motivated shift from timestamp generation to semantic-oriented approach that aligns with LLM capabilities
Comprehensive evaluation across 9 tasks spanning grounding, dense captioning, and complex reasoning domains
Strong empirical results on many benchmarks, with substantial improvements on E.T. Bench grounding (59.1-62.5 F1) and highlight detection
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 3-7) that effectively demonstrate component necessity and design choices
Clear presentation with effective figures and detailed implementation details supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: structural tokens are essentially sequence labeling, query-focused captioning is straightforward chain-of-thought, and contrastive grounding is standard. Contribution is primarily in combination rather than novel methods.

Critical dependence on external models for Query-Focused Captioning (MiniCPM-V-2.6 + GPT-4o-mini) raises reproducibility concerns and makes it unclear whether improvements come from the approach or high-quality captions

Unfair evaluation setup: previous methods designed for timestamp generation; when adapted to E.T.Instruct (Table 1), they remain competitive, contradicting the narrative that semantic approaches are inherently superior

Unresolved trade-offs undermine claims: semantic approach excels at coarse tasks but achieves R@10.7 of 23.3 vs VideoChat-T's 43.0 on fine-grained grounding; paper admits it does not 'totally replace boundary-centric approaches'
Train-inference mismatch: training uses soft contrastive loss over frames (Eq. 4) but inference uses hard frame assignment via argmax, with no analysis of this discrepancy

Architectural concessions indicate limited generalization: for dataset-wise fine-tuning, authors relax structural token temporal ordering due to dataset-specific biases (Appendix B), deviating from core temporal structure motivation

Limited analysis of learned representations: no visualization of what structural tokens attend to, no analysis of event vs. transition embeddings, minimal investigation of whether temporal structure is actually learned vs. memorized

QFC generation complexity underspecified: requires two external models; computational cost at inference not discussed; unclear if value comes from task design or caption quality (no ablation with simpler descriptions)
Generalization concerns: all training uses E.T.Instruct; zero-shot transfer limited; query-focused captioning is dataset-specific with unclear applicability elsewhere

Paper's own limitations undermine contribution: Section 6 acknowledges proposed components are 'by no means the only options for a semantic-oriented approach,' framing this as exploration rather than definitive solution

strengths: Well-motivated paradigm shift from timestamp generation to semantic-oriented approach with compelling theoretical justification about LLM capabilities
Comprehensive experimental validation: consistent improvements across 9 diverse tasks (grounding, dense captioning, complex reasoning) with particularly strong highlight detection results
Strong empirical results achieved with smaller training datasets (164K vs 900K for TRACE), demonstrating efficiency and scalability
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 5-7) that systematically validate design choices including asymmetric contrastive loss design
Excellent reproducibility: detailed implementation details, pseudocode, prompt templates, commitment to code/data release
Clear and well-written presentation with effective visualizations that clearly convey methodology
Honest acknowledgment of trade-offs and limitations rather than overselling results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: structural tokens for segmentation, contrastive learning, and captioning are established techniques combined in a relatively straightforward way

Query-focused captioning pipeline relies on external models (MiniCPM-V-2.6 + GPT-4o), adding complexity and computational overhead that is not quantified; modest gains from QFC alone (40.4 vs 38.1 F1)
Inadequate exploration of semantic vs. boundary-focused trade-off: acknowledged lower performance on fine-grained metrics (R@10.7) but insufficient investigation of when each approach is preferable
Fairness concerns in comparisons: mixed training data sizes/epochs across baselines; many results marked as non-zero-shot due to data contamination; self-implemented baselines limited
Model architecture specificity: tightly coupled to E.T.Chat; adaptations to other architectures (TimeChat, VTGLLM) required modifications; generalizability unclear
Insufficient error analysis: only 4 qualitative failure cases without frequency statistics, error type breakdown, or per-task analysis
Temporal ordering assumptions: Appendix B reveals relaxation needed for dataset-wise fine-tuning, suggesting core assumptions may not hold universally
Missing practical analysis: no computational cost comparison, inference time overhead for QFC, or scalability discussion for longer videos
